links.outcome: Deployed suicide risk model performance in transgender patient subgroup
links.effect: AUROC=0.777, AUPRC=0.115, 77% false negative rate, significant miscalibration (Brier=0.023, Spiegelhalter's z p<0.001), reducing clinical utility.
links.quote: Results indicated modest discriminative ability (AUROC=0.777, AUPRC=0.115), however, a high rate of false negatives (77%), and significant miscalibration (Brier=0.023, Spiegelhalter's z-statistic p<0.001) reduced clinical utility.

links.outcome: Discrimination, false negatives, and calibration in transgender patients
links.effect: Transgender subgroup performance: AUROC=0.777, AUPRC=0.115; false negatives 77%; significant miscalibration (Brier=0.023, Spiegelhalter's z-statistic p<0.001).
links.quote: Results indicated modest discriminative ability (AUROC=0.777, AUPRC=0.115), however, a high rate of false negatives (77%), and significant miscalibration (Brier=0.023, Spiegelhalter's z-statistic p<0.001) reduced clinical utility.

links.outcome: General-population model performance when applied to transgender patients
links.effect: The general population-trained model showed limited clinical utility in transgender patients: false negatives 77%, AUROC=0.777, AUPRC=0.115, and significant miscalibration (Brier=0.023, Spiegelhalter's z-statistic p<0.001).
links.quote: Findings underscore the importance of targeted subgroup validation and highlight limitations of general population-trained models in accurately identifying suicide risk among transgender patients.
